genZNote: Unpasteurized goat cheese is the plot twist nobody expects from a fever that keeps coming back.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Reproductive tract and mammary tissue of infected goats and sheep
habitat.hostAssociation: Zoonotic — goats and sheep are the primary reservoir for this Brucella species
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Transmitted via unpasteurized dairy products (milk, soft cheese) or direct contact with infected animal tissue/fluids

culture.media: Enriched media (blood or chocolate agar) with added CO2; requires prolonged incubation (up to several weeks)
culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate aerobe; slow-growing — cultures often held 21+ days before being called negative
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, smooth, translucent colonies appearing after several days to weeks

identificationClues: Small, Gram-negative coccobacillus, slow-growing on enriched aerobic media
History of unpasteurized dairy consumption or occupational animal exposure (farmers, veterinarians, slaughterhouse workers)
Undulant (relapsing) fever pattern with night sweats, arthralgia, and hepatosplenomegaly
Highly infectious to laboratory personnel via aerosols — requires biosafety level 3 handling

diseases: Brucellosis (undulant fever) — fever that classically waxes and wanes, night sweats, arthralgia/myalgia, hepatosplenomegaly
Can become chronic with focal complications (osteoarticular, endocarditis, neurobrucellosis)
virulenceFactors: Facultative intracellular survival within macrophages, evading immune clearance
Lipopolysaccharide with reduced endotoxic activity compared to typical Gram-negative LPS, contributing to a more indolent/chronic disease course
clinicalImportance.transmission: Ingestion of unpasteurized dairy products; direct contact with infected animal tissue, blood, or birthing fluids; occupational aerosol exposure
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Endemic in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, Central Asian, and Latin American regions where unpasteurized dairy consumption and small-ruminant husbandry are common; a significant cause of laboratory-acquired infection
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Laboratory personnel must be alerted when Brucella is suspected, since routine bench handling of cultures poses a significant aerosol-transmitted infection risk

examFacts.importantTest: Blood culture with prolonged incubation; serology (agglutination titers)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A zoonotic, facultative intracellular coccobacillus from unpasteurized goat/sheep dairy causing a classic relapsing 'undulant' fever
